text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* Northern League party leader Umberto Bossi said he might send some "observers" to attend discussions in the bi-cameral commission due to carry out constitutional reforms. The secessionist movement has until now refused to participate in the debate within the commission (all).
* A small group of Northern League supporters flew their party's flag from the top of the belltower in Venice where an armed band staged a bizarre separatist stunt 10 days ago (all).
*Education minister Luigi Berlinguer is expected to meet trade unions today after the cabinet approved a controversial plan to stem the flood of teachers seeking retirement (all).

*In an interview, Milan chief prosecutor Francesco Saverio Borrelli says the reform plan of Italy's judicial system put forward by Justice minister Giovanni Maria Flick is very interesting and calls for an end to recent clashes between magistrates and the political world. Flick took disciplinary action against a Milan magistrate who fiercely criticised the government (Corriere della Sera).

* Executives of the Foundation controlling Cariplo, Italy's largest savings bank, are due to meet today and will reportedly examine two rival offers to take part in its privatisation from Banca Commerciale Italian and Banco Ambrosiano Veneto (Repubblica, La Stampa).
** Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
